name: General Knowledge
whyItMatters: These everyday rules cover parking, freeways, emergency vehicles and your responsibilities as a driver. Getting them wrong causes fines, crashes and blocked roads.

name: Test Rules
whyItMatters: Knowledge tests only mean something if they are honest. Cheating or bribery carries serious penalties for everyone involved.

name: Alcohol & Drugs
whyItMatters: Alcohol and many drugs slow your reactions and wreck your judgement. Crashes involving alcohol are generally more serious.

name: Bicycle Safety
whyItMatters: Bike riders have no crumple zone. Giving them enough space when you pass can be the difference between a close call and a hospital visit.

name: Fatigue & Defensive Driving
whyItMatters: Tired or distracted drivers react late. Leaving space, scanning and resting keep you in control when something unexpected happens.

name: Intersections
whyItMatters: Intersections are where paths cross. Knowing exactly who gives way stops two cars arriving at the same spot at the same time.

name: Roundabouts
whyItMatters: Choosing the right lane and signalling clearly at roundabouts lets everyone predict where you are going.

name: Traffic Lights
whyItMatters: Lights share one space between many directions. Entering on red, or at the wrong time, puts you straight into another driver's path.

name: Traffic Lanes
whyItMatters: Lane lines tell everyone where traffic will be. Crossing the wrong line or merging carelessly causes side-swipes and head-on crashes.

name: Negligent Driving & Overtaking
whyItMatters: Overtaking puts you on the wrong side of the road at speed. Poor judgement here leads to the most severe crashes and heavy penalties.

name: Pedestrians
whyItMatters: People on foot are the most vulnerable road users. Children and older people in particular may not see you or may move suddenly.

name: Seat Belts & Restraints
whyItMatters: In a crash, a properly worn seat belt or child restraint is the most effective protection a passenger has.

name: Speed Limits
whyItMatters: The faster you go, the longer it takes to stop and the harder you hit. Limits are a maximum, not a target.

name: Traffic Signs
whyItMatters: Signs warn you about what you cannot see yet — a bend, a crossing, a school, a train. Reading them early buys you time.
